reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the proposed two-step thermal decoupling mechanism for noble metal HEA nanoparticles. E1 and E2 describe a single-step thermolysis of a single-source precursor, showing sequential reduction and alloying without a deliberate low-temperature nucleation hold. E3 discusses seed-mediated growth for anisotropic AuPdAg nanocrystals, which is a different material system and mechanism. None of the cited passages provide evidence for the key premises of the hypothesis.
premises: Nucleation and growth can be decoupled by a two-step thermal profile
Low-temperature incubation promotes homogeneous, metastable nucleation
High-temperature aging drives complete interdiffusion and alloying
Decoupling minimizes phase separation and elemental segregation
The mechanism applies to equimolar noble metal HEA nanoparticles under rapid heating/cooling
